## PubMed abstract

The abstract describes **17 women** receiving antidepressant therapy during breastfeeding. It reports measurement of **citalopram, sertraline, and venlafaxine** in maternal blood and breast milk; it does not state how many of the 17 women received sertraline specifically. [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30116895/)

### Drug-exposure measurement

The study measured maternal blood/serum and breast-milk antidepressant concentrations and calculated concentration-to-dose and milk-to-serum/plasma penetration ratios. For sertraline, the abstract reports no significant correlations for the examined relationships. It also reports estimated neonatal exposure as absolute infant dose for the antidepressants overall, but does not provide a sertraline-specific absolute-infant-dose value in the abstract. [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30116895/)

### Long-term developmental outcomes

The abstract reports **no long-term developmental outcomes**. It states that more data are needed to assess developmental effects. Therefore, the maternal blood and milk concentration measurements are exposure findings, not observed long-term developmental outcomes or evidence of causation. [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30116895/)

### Why these are different evidence categories

- **Milk exposure** is a measurement of sertraline in breastmilk—the potential route by which an infant may ingest the drug. LactMed reports detectable sertraline in milk in multiple studies and provides estimated infant intake from milk concentrations. This does not by itself show how much drug entered the infant’s bloodstream or whether the infant had symptoms. [S2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501191/)

- **Infant plasma detection** measures whether sertraline was detectable in an infant’s blood sample at the time tested. A detectable result indicates measured systemic exposure; a nondetectable result means the concentration was below that study’s assay threshold in that sample. It does not prove that exposure was universally absent.

- **Observed infant outcomes** are clinical observations—such as reported adverse effects, growth, development, or other findings. They are not interchangeable with drug concentrations: measured milk exposure does not establish harm, and nondetection in infant plasma does not establish zero risk. LactMed includes studies and reports with differing infant exposures and clinical observations. Its retrieved record was truncated, so later outcome material was not fully available. [S2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501191/)

### Sertraline finding in PMID 38841362

In this pharmacokinetic study of lactating women and their infants, sertraline was detectable in **all breastmilk samples**, but infant plasma sertraline was **not detectable in any of the 15 infants** tested. The infant measurement was a single plasma sample per infant, so this finding does not demonstrate zero exposure or zero risk for all infants, and it is not by itself a comprehensive assessment of clinical outcomes. [S1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38841362/)
